newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmakers to introduce expanded IRA bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmakers to introduce expanded IRA bill.

text.p: Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth said Thursday he and three other Senate and House members will unveil a bill next Wednesday to expand the features of individual retirement accounts.

"With several new features, this new IRA bill makes it even easier than our last super IRA for all Americans to save or pay for college, a first home and other critical expenses," Roth, R-Delaware, said in a statement.

"Last year, we took some first steps in expanding the IRA with the new spousal IRA. This year, expanding the IRA even further seems to be at the top of all of Washington's agenda, so I am confident that Congress and the White House can reach bipartisan agreement on this legislation and expand tax free savings to all Americans," Roth said.

Roth will be joined by Sen. John Breaux, D-Louisiana, and Reps. Bill Thomas, R-California, and Richard Neal, D-Massachusetts, at a news conference next Wednesday (1400 EST/1900 GMT) to explain the legislation.
